item.content:encoded:
They can contain it cheaply so Safe it is. And it's docile, as you noted, and not actively trying to escape. It has great potential for destruction and escape but no active desire for either.

As has been noted elsewhere on the site a nuclear bomb would be classed as safe, since it's only dangerous if someone takes it out and uses it. Same principle here; keep it fed and it's fine. And keeping it fed is even easier than keeping a normal rabbit fed, since you can throw any old junk in there. Hell, it's borderline Thaumiel, since you could use it to dispose of dangerous materials from other SCPs.

item.title: Taxonomy
item.content:encoded:
Apparently — and I can't remember where I read this, it was on some forum where people were talking about their favorite SCPs — pet rabbits are not of the species Sylvilagus bachmani. None of the Sylvilagus species are pets. They're wild North American rabbits that are terrified of humans and haven't been bred for dainty coloration and weren't imported to Australia (where Walter was found).

Pet rabbits are descended from European populations, of the genus Oryctolagus — specifically, Oryctolagus cuniculus. And, indeed, the ears in that photo are those of an Oryctolagus, not a Sylvilagus.

With that in mind, I request permission to change "Sylvilagus bachmani" in the article to "Oryctolagus cuniculus".
